title: incident-bot: slo-toolkit autodiagnostics helpers and runbook linking improvements
author: Priya Desai
ci_checks: ci/e2e: flaky on first run, rerun passed
description: Motivation: Improve automated diagnostics that the incident-bot and slo-toolkit provide during oncall incidents by adding reusable helper utilities and improving runbook linking heuristics. This PR adds a small, well-tested library of utilities used by the incident-bot to score and rank candidate runbooks, enrich SLO context with recent telemetry snapshots, and surface actionable quicklinks in oncall messages. Changes include: 1) a new slo_toolkit.autodiag.helpers module with runbook_matcher, priority_sampler, and context_enricher utilities, 2) enhancements to the incident-bot orchestrator to call the helpers when a triggered SLO alert has insufficient context, 3) lightweight telemetry snapshots captured at alert time (latency med/90/99, error-rate samples) persisted to the incident payload for improved matching, 4) a sampling policy to avoid noisy autodiagnostics for low-impact alerts, 5) CLI helper to force-run autodiagnostics for a historical incident (useful in postmortems), and 6) unit + integration tests and updated docs. Checklist: - [x] Core helpers implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] Integration wiring in incident-bot with retry/backoff - [x] Basic telemetry snapshot persisted to incident payload - [x] Sampling policy implemented and configurable via config flags - [x] E2E test against staging runbook-store and runbook search - [x] Documentation and runbook examples updated - [x] Performance sanity checked (helper runtime <50ms median) Impact: This is additive behavioral change but the default sampling thresholds are conservative; autodiagnostics are opt-in per-service via config. There are no breaking API changes. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to 10% of oncall groups for 1 week, monitor false-positive quicklinks and CPU usage, then gradual increase. Related: ENG-1823 (autodiagnostics spec), SUP-9241 (customer escalations requesting better runbook linking).
